about: The first part of the Hail Mary joins Gabriel's words (Lk 1:28) to Elizabeth's (Lk 1:42), and neither verse carries the names Maria and Iesus that the prayer supplies. The second part, the petition addressed to Mary, is of the sixteenth century.

s01.translation: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee, blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

s02.translation: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

w003.explanation: Latin says literally “full with grace”. English keeps the familiar “full of grace”.

w005.explanation: Latin leaves “est” unspoken: “Dóminus [est] tecum” — “the Lord [is] with thee”.

w007.explanation: Here too “es” remains unspoken: “benedícta [es] tu” — “blessed [art] thou”.
